questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a city in Europe that was warm and welcoming towards exchange students. I had heard that Amsterdam was a nice place to do exchange as they had good facilities for exchange students which I found to be true when I got there. Moreover, I wanted to go to a capital where I could choose interesting courses that were available in English. As University of Amsterdam strives to be a bilingual univeristy, this is also reflected in their vast course catalogue in which I found many exciting courses, and many of them were available in English.

Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The host uni provided a lot of information which helped a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance, but that was fine as I did not need it.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many options were available and UvA provided a document with an overview of all of the student housing options.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my housing there was a shared kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live with other exchange students where you can talk about your overall experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After I got my UvA mail and I logged in, it was pretty straight forward. I know that there was also a guide available, but I figured registration out before seeing this.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, a guide (PDF) of 8 pages or so was available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy and I got the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look through the course manual in time and register as soon as registration opens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had many courses, as they mostly do 6 ECTS courses at UvA. It was of course a different experience from course to course, but overall the level was suitable and very much what I was used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UvA there are more exams during the semester than what I have experienced at UCPH. The style of teaching reminded a lot of what I have experienced at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Urban Mulitilingualism 1
2. The Five Senses of Cinema
3. Modern Scandinavian Television Drama
4. Reading the City: Amsterdam Literary Classics
5. Music and Cognition

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Five Senses of Cinema was super nice and taught me a lot of new theory.

questions.answer: A lot of restaurant visits.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not approach any of these opportunities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not sure as I mostly socialized outside of uni, but there was an Erasmus group which many people at uni participated in, and they held a lof of events for exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Biking around in Amsterdam and outside of the city is amazing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other cities in the Netherlands!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, reminds a lot of DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the Erasmus groups to meet other students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Dutch people are very open and nice - and easy to talk to

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look for a place to live in good time if you do not find a place through uni.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a Swap Fiets if you're only in Amsterdam for 1 semester (a rented bike).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing social life, academic life, alone time and seeing the city.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
